newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says exports of US biotech maize a "risk".
newsitem.headline: EU says exports of US biotech maize a "risk".

text.p: Exporters shipping U.S. genetically modified maize to the European Union do so at their own risk, a European Commission spokesman said on Tuesday.

The Commission is not expected to decide until December whether to approve Ciba-Geigy AG's gene modified maize after receiving advice from EU scientific committees on food, animal feed and pesticides.
The maize, which is authorised in the U.S., has been altered to resist the corn borer pest and certain weedkillers.
"The statute is clear. Gene modified maize is not allowed on the market," Commission chief spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas told a news briefing.
Van der Pas said he did not know if any shipments containing gene modified maize had been turned back by EU member states.

Another official, noting that modified maize accounts for only two percent of the U.S. maize crop, said exporters were aware of EU rules and that there was no reason why they could not separate it from traditional maize.
The U.S. has been pressing the EU to speed up its examination of modified maize so as to allow shipments from this year's harvest. --Peter Blackburn Brussels Bureau +322 287 6830
